The New York Times asked it directly: "Sophomore slump or star potential?" Zeev Buium is 20, and Vancouver is leaning on him hard, 21.52 minutes a night and more than 24 in four of his last five games, for a team that has lost nine of its last ten. Sportsnet's headline carried coach Manny Malhotra's view: "He demands a lot of himself."

The results are what that load usually produces. He has 5 assists and no goals, and Vancouver has 36.1% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, 6.3 points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey's read on last season was similar (chances against rose with him out there), though with partners in the bottom 7%. The reason for patience is the puck: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying it in on 46% of his entries, with 28% of his shots off the rush against 17% for a typical defenseman. He assisted on Brock Boeser's 500th point Friday. Among defensemen drafted 7th to 17th since 2005 with four-plus seasons, the median first full season was 0.24 points a game; Noah Dobson, taken 12th like Buium, managed 0.21 in his.
headline: Zeev Buium, 20, learning on big minutes
